data.body: DESIGN DECISION (operator-ratified, grounded in OSS research): adopt option 2 from the ticket — DROP timeout_func_only from [tool.pytest.ini_options] so it reverts to pytest-timeout's upstream default (False), making the per-test 300 s budget cover fixture setup and teardown. Precedent: pytest-timeout's own default for func_only is False, and its README positions func_only as a last-resort workaround ('firstly make the timeouts larger'); pandas, numpy, and scikit-learn set no timeout_func_only. If dropping the key makes any slow-fixture test trip the budget, the remedy is to RAISE that test's timeout via @pytest.mark.timeout(N) (the README-sanctioned remedy), never to restore func_only. REJECTED: option 1 session_timeout — it is cooperative (checked between tests), cannot stop a hanging test, and the README says it complements per-test timeouts, never substitutes. REJECTED: option 3 targeted per-fixture guards — no ecosystem precedent. The 300 s budget already DWARFS the slowest legitimate call time (29.93 s), so charging fixture time to the first requesting test carries low trip risk.
